title: Tool.RequiresHandle / the Handle part
summary: Tools attach to the player's hand through a part named exactly 'Handle'. With RequiresHandle=true (default) a missing/misnamed Handle means the tool won't hold correctly. Name it 'Handle', case-sensitive.

properties.name: RequiresHandle
properties.description: Whether the tool needs a 'Handle' part to be holdable.

properties.name: GripPos / GripForward / GripUp / GripRight
properties.description: How the Handle sits in the hand (advanced positioning).

explanation.whatItIs: The handshake between tool and character: the engine welds a specially-named part to the hand.
explanation.whyItExists: Roblox needs ONE agreed-upon part to weld; the convention is a direct child named 'Handle'.
whenToUse: Every visual tool: include a Handle part (the mesh/visual can be welded TO it)
Handle-less tools (magic auras, UI tools): RequiresHandle = false
whenNotToUse: Renaming the handle to anything else — the weld breaks
tips: Build visuals as children welded to Handle for complex shapes
Grip* properties fine-tune hand position without moving geometry
commonMistakes: Naming it 'handle' or 'Grip' — must be exactly 'Handle'
Handle not a DIRECT child of the Tool

examples.title: Correct tool structure
examples.code:
-- Explorer structure:
-- Wand (Tool)
--  ├─ Handle (Part)        ← required name, direct child
--  └─ Crystal (Part)       ← welded to Handle

local crystal = script.Parent.Crystal
local handle = script.Parent.Handle
local weld = Instance.new("WeldConstraint")
weld.Part0 = handle
weld.Part1 = crystal
weld.Parent = handle
